limitations: No live Feishu WebSocket, official Lark SDK, OpenClaw RPC or maintenance-window action was exercised.
Passing tests are component-level offline evidence, not a consumer-cutover or production acceptance result.

findings.title: Gateway directly dispatches Analyzer and bypasses OpenClaw orchestration
findings.risk: Violates the two-message intent protocol and prevents OpenClaw from owning policy, queueing, cancellation, recovery and GPU scheduling.
findings.required_disposition: Production Gateway must forward normalized ingress only; OpenClaw must create a valid reply-bound analysis_request and dispatch Analyzer work.

findings.title: Signature verification is optional and defaults to accept
findings.risk: A future real adapter can feed unsigned or forged events into ingress/RPC/analysis paths if a verifier is omitted.
findings.required_disposition: Require official signature and timestamp verification at production factory construction and fail startup if it is absent.

findings.title: Group-only session key can mix users
findings.risk: All senders in one group share an OpenClaw session unless the unverified RPC layer overrides it.
findings.required_disposition: Adopt a versioned account/channel/chat/sender session namespace by default, with explicit tested opt-in for shared group sessions.

findings.title: Single-consumer control is simulated only
findings.risk: No lease, fence or live connection verification prevents overlap or a no-consumer gap during migration.
findings.required_disposition: Implement an operator-authorized fenced consumer lease and live owner/socket/event proof before cutover.

findings.title: RPC placeholder embeds unverified protocol semantics
findings.risk: Hard-coded method names and fields can be incompatible with the official RPC surface and hide orchestration responsibilities in Gateway.
findings.required_disposition: Create a versioned adapter from an approved official RPC probe, with documented auth, capability, cancellation, correlation and idempotency semantics.

findings.title: Retry and JSON state handling can produce duplicate work
findings.risk: Ambiguous RPC outcomes, concurrent processes or interrupted in-place state writes can duplicate work or lose dedupe/ticket state.
findings.required_disposition: Use transactional durable event/outbox state, end-to-end idempotency keys, atomic transitions, retention and one typed retry policy.

findings.title: Runbook omits durable handoff and recovery proof
findings.risk: The documented stop/start sequence cannot demonstrate no loss, no duplicate consumption, restored state, or bounded rollback time.
findings.required_disposition: Add quiesce/drain, boundary ids, backup/restore hashes, replay reconciliation, owner command and measured RTO/RPO acceptance.

findings.title: Secret, log and report protections are partial
findings.risk: Generic reports remain trackable and have no enforced redaction check; the current branch has no commits, so history cannot be audited.
findings.required_disposition: Enforce report/diagnostic redaction in CI or pre-commit and test it with masked secret and identifier fixtures.

findings.title: Error policy and readiness signals are incomplete
findings.risk: Operators cannot reliably classify retryability, ambiguity, split-brain or consumer staleness.
findings.required_disposition: Unify typed error mapping, bounded backoff and readiness metrics for owner identity, lease, event age and queue state.

findings.title: Synchronous Analyzer dispatch cannot scale GPU work
findings.risk: GPU work can block event flow and is not centrally queued, cancelled or serialized.
findings.required_disposition: OpenClaw must own queued job lifecycle; Analyzer workers must obtain the shared GPU lock and persist job status.

findings.title: Account and channel namespaces are absent
findings.risk: Additional Feishu apps/accounts or channels can collide in identity, session and consumer ownership.
findings.required_disposition: Adopt a normalized envelope with channel, account/tenant, adapter version and stable external ids.

findings.title: Ticket and dedupe retention are unbounded
findings.risk: Long-running state growth makes recovery files larger despite correct expiry/replay rejection.
findings.required_disposition: Add bounded retention and compaction tests.

findings.title: Lifecycle scripts trust reusable PIDs
findings.risk: A stale PID/status file does not prove process or consumer ownership.
findings.required_disposition: Verify process command identity and fenced lease before lifecycle actions.

retained_controls: Offline-only runtime and false readiness without verified transports.
Environment-reference configuration and ignored runtime/credential paths.
Quarantine and SHA-256 validation with Analyzer raw-path rejection.
Hashed identifier logs, one-time ticket binding, and local duplicate-event coverage.
Reply-bound analysis_request tests for identity, expiry, hash and idempotency.
architecture_pass_blockers: Remove direct Gateway-to-Analyzer dispatch and prove OpenClaw-owned reply-to analysis flow.
Verify and version the official OpenClaw RPC adapter.
Prevent cross-user session sharing by documented tested policy.
Prove a fenced, observable single-consumer cutover with durable recovery.
Add transactional event/job state, GPU orchestration and report-redaction enforcement.
